name: Cold-chain logistics

problems.words: Temperature logs are filled by hand at the end of the shift
quick_ideas: Set fixed reading times on the log, so readings reflect the real time
Ask for a photo of the display at each reading, so records can be trusted.

workzap_build.text: You would see temperature readings arrive from sensors in each chamber on their own, so a complete record exists without anyone filling in logs by hand.

problems.ask_first: Do staff fill the logs from memory at shift end, or from readings noted on paper during the day?
problems.free_stops: How readings are captured and stored is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the reading times written on each hand log with actual shift timings this week, so backfilled entries are easy to spot.
Make one shift lead collect and review every hand log before staff leave, so entries get written during the workday.

problems.words: We found out about a compressor failure only in the morning
quick_ideas: Assign a named person to night temperature rounds, so someone is watching
Keep a night technician's contact on hand.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp alarms to the on-duty person when a reading goes out of range, escalating automatically if not acknowledged.

problems.ask_first: Do the chambers have any sensor or meter that records readings now?
problems.free_stops: Alarm levels and escalation rules are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write down when the last normal temperature was seen each night this week, so the blind hours before morning become visible.
Give one night person the job of noting one overnight equipment check in a single notebook, so failures are noticed before day staff arrive.

problems.words: Client claims goods spoiled in our store and we have no records
quick_ideas: Keep temperature records and gate passes for each lot together, so evidence is ready
Photograph goods' condition on receipt.

workzap_build.text: A claim file per incident that collects temperature records, photos and handover notes automatically.

problems.ask_first: Is the dispute usually about temperature during storage, or about the condition of goods on arrival?
problems.free_stops: What goes into each claim file is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check one disputed lot from receipt to dispatch on paper this week, so you see exactly which proof is missing.
Keep one folder per client for receipts, storage notes and dispatch papers, so claim discussions start with a complete paper trail.

problems.words: Load-shedding means the generator runs half the day
quick_ideas: Log generator hours and diesel daily for a week, so you know the real cost
Note which chambers draw most.

workzap_build.text: A power and generator log with hours, diesel and cost per day and per chamber.

problems.ask_first: Does the generator run through the working day, or mostly through the evening and night?
problems.free_stops: How costs are split per chamber is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note generator start and stop times beside chamber activity for one week, so you see which operating hours drive the longest runs.
Give one person the job of writing every outage and generator run in one notebook, so fuel-heavy periods stop being argued from memory.

problems.words: We don't know which chamber has whose goods
quick_ideas: Draw a chamber map of where each client's lots sit, so goods can be found
Tag each lot with its date in.

workzap_build.text: A chamber-wise stock register by client role, lot, units and date in, with a location map.

problems.ask_first: Do you lose track of goods right after unloading, or when lots are moved between chambers later?
problems.free_stops: The register layout is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk each chamber and note any lot whose client cannot be identified at a glance, so the search problem has a clear size.
Assign one store hand to update a single chamber notebook whenever goods move, so every team member checks the same place.

problems.words: Clients' bags or crates go missing or get mixed up
quick_ideas: Issue a gate pass for every withdrawal, signed by the client's representative
Count a few clients' lots this week, so you see where gaps are.

workzap_build.text: You would have a gate pass for every lot going in and out, tied to each client's stock, so you can see who took what and when.

problems.ask_first: Do crates go missing at withdrawal time, or get mixed up when stored together?
problems.free_stops: The gate pass flow is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare what is written at receipt with what is physically present for a few selected client lots, so mix-ups show where they start.
Give one dispatch person the job of updating one withdrawal list before any goods leave, so missing crates are caught at the door.

problems.words: Clients take goods out but rent calculations are disputed
quick_ideas: Send each client a statement of units and days stored, so disputes start from facts
Agree rent units in writing.

workzap_build.text: A rent calculator by unit and days stored that produces client statements and tracks balances.

problems.ask_first: Is the dispute over how many days were counted, or over how many units were charged?
problems.free_stops: How rent is calculated is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Review a few recent exits and note where stored days or units were unclear on paper, so billing disputes can be traced to the source.
Make one clerk maintain a single running list of entries and exits for chargeable storage, so rent calculations use one version.

problems.words: Restaurants complain frozen deliveries arrive soft
quick_ideas: Ask drivers for a photo of the reefer display at each drop, so you see where temperature slips
Plan multi-drop order so doors open as little as possible.

workzap_build.text: A reefer trip log with temperature trace and door-open events per delivery.

problems.ask_first: Do frozen deliveries arrive soft on long multi-drop routes, or even on short single deliveries?
problems.free_stops: What the trip log records is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which delivery routes return the most soft-product complaints this week, so the trouble pattern is tied to a route not guesswork.
Give one dispatcher the job of recording departure and return times for frozen loads in one place, so delays affecting deliveries are easier to pin down.

problems.words: The store is full in potato season and empty half the year
quick_ideas: Note occupancy by month for last year, so you see the empty months clearly
List possible off-season clients.

workzap_build.text: A seasonal capacity planner using past occupancy by month.

problems.ask_first: Is the store empty mostly because one crop fills it, or because regular clients pull out after the season?
problems.free_stops: How the planner forecasts is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark full and quiet weeks from your last year notebook on one page, so the slack periods are clear in your own records.
Give one person the job of updating a weekly occupancy page all year, so busy and empty periods are tracked the same way.

problems.words: I can't see temperature across all sites from my phone
quick_ideas: Ask each site for one temperature report a day, so you have a baseline
Agree what counts as an alarm worth calling you.

workzap_build.text: An owner phone view across sites: temperatures, alarms, occupancy and receivables.

problems.ask_first: Are your sites in one city, or spread across several cities and provinces?
problems.free_stops: What the owner view includes is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the latest reading time and temperature reported from each site on one page daily, so late or missing updates stand out.
Give one supervisor the job of sending the owner's daily site summary at a fixed hour, so you stop chasing scattered updates.

never_say: Whether spoiled or out-of-range goods are safe to sell or use; food safety or pharma professionals decide.
Help editing temperature logs, re-dating or relabelling goods.
Pharma GDP, HACCP or food safety standards; refrigeration engineering or generator sizing.
Views on insurance or legal claims over spoilage.
Storing client and staff details. For ammonia or refrigerant leaks, fire, or someone trapped in a cold room, emergency services come first.

sample_reply.person: Pichle hafte raat ko ek chamber ka compressor band ho gaya aur subah pata chala. Aisa dobara na ho, koi tareeqa batao.
sample_reply.pi:
Ji haan, ye theek ho sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, raat ke temperature round ke liye ek banda muqarrar karein, taake koi zimmedaar dekh raha ho.
Doosra, raat ke liye technician ka number har waqt maujood rakhein, taake masla hote hi rabta ho sake.
Workzap is ke liye ye bana sakta hai: reading had se bahar jaye to duty wale ko WhatsApp alarm jaye, aur jawab na aaye to agla banda apne aap alert ho.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
